slides.title: Ropedia raises $22M to scale human-centric data collection for embodied AI
slides.tldr: FUNDING FOR EMBODIED AI DATA COLLECTION
slides.highlight: Ropedia is scaling human-centric data collection for embodied AI, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Towards Agentic Agent-based Models: Feasibility, Performance, and Statistical Model Checking
slides.tldr: INTEGRATING LLM-BASED AGENTS INTO ABM SIMULATIONS
slides.highlight: This research explores replacing symbolic rules in agent-based models with LLM-driven decisions, which is relevant to MIMIC's use of LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: Investigates the feasibility and performance of replacing symbolic rules in agent-based models with LLM-driven tool calls.
card.key_idea: Extends the Schelling segregation model by delegating one agent's neighbor classification to a local LLM (Qwen3.5) using tool calls to update similarity counters.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using robustness checks (semantic/operational) and statistical model checking via MultiVeStA to compare transient trajectories of happy agents against the original model.
card.limitation: Small LLMs exhibit semantic errors and operational failures; larger models are reliable but introduce significant runtime overhead.

slides.title: MeetingToM: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs on Theory-of-Mind Reasoning in Multi-Party Meetings
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR MULTIMODAL THEORY-OF-MIND IN MEETINGS
slides.highlight: This work introduces MeetingToM to evaluate MLLMs on latent social states, addressee understanding, and group consensus, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: MeetingToM is a multimodal benchmark evaluating MLLMs' Theory-of-Mind reasoning in complex, multi-party meeting scenarios.
card.key_idea: A hierarchical evaluation framework testing subject-level mental states, dyadic referential intent/attitudes, and group-level consensus, specifically targeting 'pseudo-consensus' where non-verbal cues mask verbal agreement.
card.evaluation: Evaluated proprietary (GPT-5, Gemini-3 Pro) and open-source (Qwen) MLLMs using 1,800 AMI Corpus clips; humans significantly outperformed models across all tasks.
card.limitation: Limited to English-language meetings, short video segments (5s/50s) rather than full meetings, and lacks direct participant self-reported mental states.

slides.title: Teachy Mini: Development and Preliminary Evaluation of a Knowledge-Based Generative Social Robot for Higher Education
slides.tldr: KNOWLEDGE-BASED GENERATIVE SOCIAL ROBOT FOR TUTORING
slides.highlight: This work explores how knowledge-based design and large language models can create responsible tutoring behaviors in social robots, contributing to RwB's focus on AI-mediated embodied learning.

card.one_liner: Teachy Mini is a generative social robot using Knowledge-Based Design to provide responsible, personalized tutoring in higher education.
card.key_idea: Operationalizes KBD requirements via dynamic system prompting, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for lecture slides, and stateful prompt orchestration to adapt to learner states.
card.evaluation: Between-subjects study (N=24) comparing KBD vs. control robots using knowledge tests, TAM scales, and a custom Responsible Behavior scale.
card.limitation: Preliminary evaluation with a small sample size (N=24) and a single-session interaction context.

slides.title: StARS: Socially Appropriate Robot Actions via a Recommender System-Driven Approach
slides.highlight: StARS uses a recommender system-driven approach to generate user-specific appropriateness scores for robot actions, supporting the RwB goal of embodied social robots that align with individual user norms.

card.one_liner: StARS uses a recommender system approach to personalize socially appropriate robot actions based on individual user preferences.
card.key_idea: A model-agnostic framework integrating collaborative filtering (matrix factorization) with learnable scene representations via residual fusion to predict user-specific appropriateness scores for candidate robot actions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on MannersDB+ and SocNav1 using various backbones (MLPs, GNNs). Results show statistically significant improvements in RMSE/MSE, Pearson r, and CCC.

slides.title: Modeling turn-taking with distant viewing: investigating silence thresholds in human and AI-generated discourse
slides.tldr: SILENCE THRESHOLDS IN HUMAN AND AI DISCOURSE
slides.highlight: This study analyzes silence gaps in human and AI-generated audiovisual material, providing insights into turn-taking dynamics relevant to HyECHO's focus on engagement and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: Study compares silence thresholds in human sitcoms versus AI-generated synthetic podcasts.
card.key_idea: Analysis of silence gaps across speaker gender and production settings using fundamental-frequency thresholds estimated in Praat.
card.evaluation: Analyzed thirty US situational comedies and fifty-one Google NotebookLM synthetic podcasts; results' trustworthiness not clearly stated.

slides.title: ACME: A Multi-Cultural, Multi-Embodiment Social-Navigation Dataset
slides.highlight: This dataset captures diverse human-robot interactions across different cultures and robot embodiments, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: ACME is a large-scale, multi-cultural, multi-embodiment dataset for social robot navigation and pedestrian trajectory prediction.
card.key_idea: Data collected across 5 countries using 7 robot types, featuring onboard multi-modal sensors, robot speech interactions, and human-verified BEV pedestrian trajectories.
card.evaluation: Compared against prior datasets via qualitative/quantitative analysis of scenario complexity and pedestrian behavior; benchmarked SOTA vision navigation and trajectory prediction models.
card.limitation: Anonymization requirements across different institutions led to varying levels of information loss in RGB data.

slides.title: Imitation of Arm Gestures by the Semi-Humanoid Robot NICO
slides.tldr: HUMAN ARM GESTURE IMITATION FOR SEMI-HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This research develops a system for a semi-humanoid robot to imitate human arm gestures using a pose-estimation model and analytical geometry, contributing to the goals of RwB regarding human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A system for the NICO robot to imitate human arm gestures using monocular RGB input.
card.key_idea: Combines MediaPipe pose and hand landmark extraction with analytical geometric formulas to compute joint angles, which are then linearly mapped to NICO's motor configurations.
card.evaluation: Tested with six participants performing 11 poses across three viewing angles. Results show moderate accuracy for most joints, with MAEs between 10° and 34°.
card.limitation: High reconstruction error for forearm rotation (50.1° MAE) and sensitivity to self-occlusion in complex poses.

slides.title: Italian Startup Debuts Gene.01 Humanoid With Skin That Senses Humans Before Contact
slides.highlight: The Gene.01 humanoid features skin capable of sensing humans before contact, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Bounding the Causal Impact of ML-assisted Decision-Making via Counterfactual Correctness
slides.tldr: BOUNDING CAUSAL IMPACT OF ML DECISIONS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a partial-identification approach to bound the causal effect of new ML models using prior RCT data, supporting MIMIC's focus on impact analysis of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: A method to bound the causal impact of new ML models using prior RCT data and predictive accuracy.
card.key_idea: Uses partial identification with monotonicity assumptions on 'counterfactual correctness' (correct predictions don't harm outcomes) and subgroup performance to bound outcomes of untrialed models.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a semi-synthetic simulation study; results showed more informative bounds compared to prior work.
card.limitation: Requires 'true labels' to be observed for all RCT individuals and assumes predictions do not influence those labels.

slides.title: Motion Primitive Discovery in a Humanoid Robot via Self-Organising Maps for Phase Recognition
slides.tldr: MOTOR PRIMITIVE DISCOVERY VIA SOM AND ESN
slides.highlight: This work proposes an architecture for motor primitive discovery and online phase recognition in a humanoid robot, contributing to the understanding of action recognition in human-robot interaction for RwB.

card.one_liner: A two-level MNS-inspired architecture for online movement phase recognition in a humanoid robot.
card.key_idea: Two Self-Organising Maps (SOMs) discover arm and hand motion primitives, which an Echo State Network (ESN) then integrates temporally to recognize movement phases.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 4,200 simulated NICO robot trials across seven actions. The ESN achieved 93.9% phase recognition accuracy using only SOM primitives.
card.limitation: Trained and evaluated only on the robot's own actions; lacks cross-embodiment observation capabilities.

slides.title: Computational models of pragmatic reasoning with flexible generation of meaning and expression alternatives
slides.highlight: The SAGE framework combines language models with rule-based selectors to model how interlocutors reason over alternative expressions and interpretations, supporting HyECHO's goals in addressee and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: SAGE combines language model flexibility with rule-based task analysis to model pragmatic reasoning over open-ended alternatives.
card.key_idea: A neuro-symbolic framework using LM-based 'proposers' for alternatives and 'evaluators' for assessment, coordinated by symbolic 'selectors' implementing cognitively motivated task analyses.
card.evaluation: Tested via three case studies (referential expressions, M-implicatures, Gricean implicatures) using ablations, baseline comparisons, and quantitative fit to human data.
card.limitation: LM evaluators struggle with formal/theoretical measures, performing better on intuitive judgments than on rigorous semantic or logical inference.

slides.title: OPPO Launches Xiaobu Next Beta with On-Device Multi-Agent System
slides.highlight: The debut of an on-device multi-agent system on smartphones provides a practical implementation of agent-based interactions relevant to MIMIC's focus on hybrid human-AI societies.

slides.title: Towards Reducing Foreign Language Anxiety Using Level-Appropriate Embodied Conversational Agents
slides.tldr: LEVEL-APPROPRIATE EMBODIED CONVERSATIONAL AGENTS FOR SLA
slides.highlight: This work proposes a multi-agent system that generates level-appropriate dialogue to reduce foreign language anxiety, contributing to HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement in human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: A multi-agent system generating CEFR level-appropriate dialogue to help reduce foreign language anxiety in learners.
card.key_idea: A "generate-evaluate-regenerate" loop using multiple LLM agents and a level classifier to adapt dialogue simplicity to user proficiency.
card.evaluation: Pilot study with Japanese university students; 87.4% of output matched CEFR levels versus 54.1% for unsimplified agents.
card.limitation: Small sample size resulted in no statistically significant evidence that the system reduces foreign language anxiety levels.
